turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. I guess what made me come in is that... well, the things that usually make me feel like myself just started feeling really flat and heavy lately. Like my photography walks, for instance. I usually go out every Sunday. I actually still shoot on 35mm film, which is getting incredibly expensive to develop these days. The lab I use downtown just raised their prices again last month, and the guy who runs it—Frank, I think his name is, or maybe Fred—he was telling me it's because of all these supply chain issues with the silver halide chemicals. It's a whole ordeal just to get a roll of Kodak Gold processed now. 

But anyway... yeah, the photography, and mentoring the kids at the youth center... even just keeping a clean calendar at work. I'm an executive assistant, so my whole life is color-coded calendars, you know? But recently, I just... I stopped initiating any of it. It all just feels too heavy to even start.

turns.doctor_question: Over these past 14 months since your brother's health changed, has the heavy, flat feeling been constant the whole time, or have there been periods—maybe weeks or longer—where you felt more like your normal self again?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it hasn't been completely constant, no. For most of this whole period, I've actually been cycling back into these... these stretches where I'm incredibly driven. Like, overconfident, almost? Actually, during one of those stretches last spring, I decided I was going to reorganize the entire physical filing system at the office. We still have these massive metal filing cabinets from the 90s—the really heavy ones that look like they belong in a bunker? I don't know why we haven't digitized everything yet. My boss keeps saying it's a security thing, but I think he just likes the aesthetic of paper. Anyway, I stayed late for like three nights in a row, color-coding thousands of manila folders. In August, it feels like a swamp in there, and then by November, you're wearing a parka at your desk. They say they're going to upgrade the HVAC system, but they've been saying that since 2018. 

But yeah, I'd have these periods where I just felt like I could conquer the world on three hours of sleep, and then eventually, I'd crash back into that heavy, flat feeling again.

turns.doctor_question: During those stretches where you felt overconfident and barely slept—like when you were reorganizing the filing system—did you experience anything unusual like hearing voices, seeing things, or having beliefs that others around you thought were strange? Or did anyone express serious concern about your behavior during those times?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, actually... when I get into those high-energy stretches, running on, you know, barely any sleep, things do get a little... intense. Like, I get this overwhelming certainty that the way things are arranged—like calendar problems or emails bouncing back—they mean something special. Like there's a hidden message just for me. And sometimes, when I'm really pushing it and not sleeping, I'll hear these... short comments. Just quick voices, like someone is right there, commenting on what I'm doing. 

It's actually kind of like how our office intercom system used to act up. Have I told you about that? We have this ancient system from the 80s, the kind with the little plastic buttons that light up amber when someone is paging you. For a while, it was picking up interference from a local radio station, I swear. You'd be sitting there trying to draft an agenda for the board meeting, and suddenly you'd hear the faint sound of a used car commercial coming through the speaker on your phone. My boss thought I was making it up until he heard it himself during a conference call with the regional director. The director was not amused, let me tell you. He's this very stern guy who wears suspenders every day—like, who wears suspenders anymore unless you're a lumberjack or a hipster? Anyway, we had to get the telecom guy out there, and he spent four hours in the server closet just to tell us the wiring was unshielded. Typical. But yeah, during those high stretches, the feeling about the messages gets really strong, and I do hear those little comments sometimes.
